text.p: Colombian Defense Minister Guillermo Alberto Gonzalez announced he was stepping down on Sunday, just two days after revealing that his 1989 Congress campaign received a check signed by a reputed drug kingpin.

Gonzalez, speaking to the Caracol radio network, said he had tendered his resignation to President Ernesto Samper on the grounds that the budding campaign finance scandal had undermined his credibity and made it impossible for him to continue in the job he was appointed to only in January.
"I find that I can no longer dedicate 100 percent of my time to resolving the country's problems," Gonzalez, who was Samper's third defense minister, told Caracol.

Samper's first defense minister, Fernando Botero, has been held at a military base in the capital since August 1995 on charges stemming from his involvement in the embattled president's scandal-plagued 1994 election campaign.
Gonzalez has insisted that he is free of any wrongdoing, since at the time his campaign aides accepted a $3,000 donation from Justo Pastor Perafan there were no criminal charges against Perafan.

Gonzalez has acknowledged having social dealings with Perafan in the past, however, and senior military officials refused to voice support for him in public after his revelation about the campaign contribution. Drug-related "illicit enrichment" charges were filed against Perafan in February of last year and he has been the target of a nationwide manhunt ever since.
